output.evaluation_note: While 'hoàn toàn' (完全) shares the same Hán-Việt root as Japanese '完全' and can mean 'complete' or 'absolute' (aligning with part of the English definition 'complete'), its primary adjectival usage in modern Vietnamese does not naturally convey the 'perfect' (flawless, ideal) sense. For 'perfect' in this sense, 'hoàn hảo' or 'tuyệt vời' would be more appropriate. The proposed 'hoàn toàn' is semantically too narrow for the full scope of the English 'perfect' and Japanese '完全', leading to potential learner confusion as a false friend for the 'flawless' aspect.
